sections.heading: What Is Curtain Wall Repair and Why Does It Matter in Tysons?
sections.body: A curtain wall is a non-structural glazing system that forms the exterior skin of a building, typically made of aluminum framing and large glass panels. These systems are common throughout Tysons, where modern office towers, luxury residential buildings, and corporate campuses rely on them for aesthetic appeal and environmental performance. Over time, curtain wall systems can develop failed seals, cracked or broken glass panels, corroded framing, and compromised gaskets — all of which can lead to water infiltration, drafts, and visible damage. In a dense commercial corridor like Tysons, a poorly maintained facade not only affects tenant satisfaction but can signal deferred maintenance to prospective clients and occupants. Timely curtain wall repair helps preserve the building envelope, prevent interior water damage, and keep the exterior looking sharp. Our team diagnoses issues accurately and delivers targeted repairs that address root causes rather than just surface symptoms.

sections.heading: Common Curtain Wall Problems We Repair Near Tysons Corner and The Boro
sections.body: Curtain wall systems fail in predictable ways, and our technicians are trained to identify and resolve the full range of issues that affect commercial buildings in the Tysons market. Cracked or shattered glass panels are among the most visible problems, often caused by thermal stress, impact, or building movement. Failed or deteriorated silicone sealant is another frequent culprit, allowing water and air to penetrate the system at joints and transitions. Aluminum framing can become corroded or misaligned over time, especially on older buildings near high-traffic areas like the Tysons Corner Metro station or the dense retail and office clusters around International Drive. We also repair damaged gaskets, replace failed infill panels, and address structural silicone bonding issues. Whether your building has a stick-built, unitized, or semi-unitized curtain wall system, we have the experience and equipment to perform safe, effective repairs at height using proper access methods.

sections.heading: Our Curtain Wall Repair Process for Commercial Properties
sections.body: Every curtain wall repair engagement begins with a thorough visual and hands-on inspection of the affected area. Our team reviews the extent of glass damage, sealant failure, framing condition, and any signs of water intrusion before recommending a repair scope. We provide clear documentation of findings so that property managers and building owners can make informed decisions. Once the scope is approved, we coordinate access — whether that involves lifts, scaffolding, or rope access — to reach panels safely on mid-rise and high-rise buildings common throughout Tysons. Replacement glass is sourced to match existing specifications including thickness, tint, and coating where possible. Sealant work is performed using professional-grade materials appropriate for exterior glazing applications. We work efficiently to minimize disruption to building occupants and complete projects within agreed timelines. Upon completion, we walk clients through the work performed and ensure satisfaction before closing out the job.

faq.q: How do I know if my curtain wall system needs repair?
faq.a: Common signs include visible cracks or breaks in glass panels, water stains or moisture inside the building near exterior walls, drafts near glazing, discolored or missing sealant at joints, and condensation between glass layers. A professional inspection can confirm the extent of damage and identify the best repair approach.

faq.q: Can you match the existing glass on my building in Tysons?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. We work to source replacement glass that matches the original specifications as closely as possible, including thickness, color, tint, and surface coatings. Exact matching depends on the original glass specifications and current product availability, which we assess during the inspection and planning phase.

faq.q: Do you handle both emergency repairs and planned maintenance projects?

We respond to emergency glass failures that require immediate boarding or temporary weatherproofing, and we also plan and execute scheduled repair projects for property managers and building owners who want to address curtain wall issues as part of routine maintenance or capital improvement programs.
